study_identification_part.si_4_title: Multiscale heterogeneity of functional connectivity in autism

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Gaussian process regression was used to fit separate normative models to each of 75,855 FC estimates. The method allows for non-linear models that can adaptively fit complex datasets. The normative model was trained on neurotypical individuals and tested on autistic individuals. Deviations were calculated by subtracting predicted from observed FC and dividing by estimated variance.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We used gaussian process regression, as described by (Marquand et al., 2016), to fit separate normative models to each of 75,855 FC estimates between each pair of 390 brain regions, using age, sex, and mean framewise displacement. This method allows for the calculation of non-linear models that can adaptively fit complex datasets.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Ilioska2024.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Normative modeling

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Resting-state functional connectivity (FC) between 390 brain regions (400 Schaefer cortical parcels minus 24 excluded regions plus 15 Harvard-Oxford subcortical ROIs), resulting in 75,855 pairwise FC estimates per participant. FC was computed using Pearson correlations between regional average time series, normalized using Gaussian-gamma mixture modeling.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: To map inter-regional FC, we used the well-validated Schaefer parcellation (Schaefer et al., 2018) to obtain 400 functional cortical regions of interest (ROIs) for each participant. We also included 15 subcortical ROIs from the Harvard-Oxford subcortical atlas... A total of 24 regions were excluded due to low coverage (<70% coverage in >5% of the participants) leaving 390 regions remaining for analysis... We used Pearson correlations to calculate the relationship between each pair of regional average time series.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Ilioska2024.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Mapping functional connectivity

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Three explanatory variables were used in the normative model: age (linear term), sex, and mean framewise displacement (head motion parameter). Site effects were addressed separately using ComBat harmonization prior to normative modeling rather than being included as a covariate in the model.
